articles.title: China’s first AI-generated film is a flop. Some still see it as the future of cinema
articles.summary: Chinese investors placing high value on AI despite unpopularity of Sanxingdui: Future Past. China’s first fully AI-generated movie has flopped, earning just 1.7m yuan (£191,000) at the box office despite costing “tens of millions” to make, according to its producer. But is it any good?
body: But is it any good? The Guardian watched Sanxingdui: Future Past in a virtually empty cinema in Beijing, and found it no worse than plenty of human-centred mindless action flicks.

Sanxingdui tells a confusing tale of a future society in which every decision has been outsourced to algorithms and AI, leading to a global catastrophe. The only way to avert the impending doom is to unlock the hidden code that is hidden in the Sanxingdui, bronze sculptures linked to the ancient kingdom of Shu. Cue astronauts racing through ancient Egypt and archeologists diving through space-time vortices.
All of the film’s visuals and some of its sound effects were created using AI, while it was edited by humans.

articles.title: Mum, I’m Alien Pregnant review – slime and silliness in amusing New Zealand comedy horror
articles.summary: Mucus, alien gristle, a tentacle-bearing penis and, of course, the pregnancy of the title are all borne with deadpan calmness in this underplayed comedy. In this amusingly silly exercise in gross-out body horror and bathos from New Zealand, thirtysomething underachiever Mary (Hannah Lynch) finds…
body: Fortunately, the cast is well up for serving this sort of underplayed comedy, especially supporting players Yvette Parsons and Jackie van Beek, as Mary and Arlo’s single mums Cynthia and Ann respectively. For example, somewhere towards the end (and don’t worry, there’s nothing to spoil here), Cynthia gets a little het up about Mary farting too much, after a nest of mucus, tissue and alien gristle shoots out of Mary’s nether regions. Ann, on the other hand, gets quite concerned about the mess all this is making of her immaculate flat, and keeps apologising for the disorder to anyone who shows up, including unflappable paramedics Sofia (Karen O’Leary) and Sophie (Ariadne Baltazar).

Is it all meant to be a parable about the anxieties of single motherhood and the changes pregnancy wreaks on the female body? Yes, sure, if you want. But subtext is less the point than slow burns and slime, and that honest directness make the end result rather winning.

articles.title: Andrew Scott drama Elsinore leads British independent film award nominations
articles.summary: Elsinore is in contention for 12 Bifas, including for Scott’s highly praised performance, while Clio Barnard’s I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning, Ashley Walters’ Animol and Mike Leigh’s Tender Loving Care are also recognised.
body: Elsinore, the drama in which Andrew Scott plays the actor Ian Charleson as he takes on Shakespeare’s Hamlet in the last months of his life, before he died of Aids in 1990, has emerged as the leading contender for the British independent film awards (Bifas).

The film, which is directed by Simon Stone and co-stars Olivia Colman, Billie Piper and Johnny Flynn, received 12 nominations, including best British independent film, best director for Stone and best lead performance for Scott. Elsinore has collected rave reviews since its premiere at the Telluride film festival in September, with the Guardian’s Benjamin Lee describing it as “a devastating movie [that] is a reminder of Charleson’s strength and the many men like him and it implores us to remember them too”. Scott is also already being tipped as the favourite for the best actor Oscar – and he would be the first out gay actor to win.

articles.title: Ghost Town review – the phantoms and lost souls haunting a Japanese city after the 2011 earthquake
articles.summary: Katharine Round’s documentary puts cameras in taxis where drivers and fares reflect on the disaster’s impact and talk of crowds of spectres and disappearing passengers.
body: I n a manner similar to Ryūsuke Hamaguchi’s Drive My Car, in which journeying lulls passengers into greater intimacy, this nocturnal taxi odyssey through the tsunami-hit city of Kamaishi on Japan’s east coast clears the road for the subconscious to manifest. Conversations between the drivers and their customers drift back towards the cataclysm of the 2011 earthquake and tsunami with an undertow of grief, loss and absence. But at least this time there’s someone in the rear-view mirror to converse with; some drivers claim to have picked up phantom fares who later vanished from the back seat.

articles.title: Tristan Thompson Boards Jason Zada’s Bitcoin Creator Movie ‘Satoshi’ as Producer (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: A new feature film titled “Satoshi,” about Bitcoin’s pseudonymous creator Satoshi Nakamoto, is set to be directed by Jason Zada (“The Forest, “Terrarium”) with backing from former NBA champion and tech investor Tristan Thompson.
body: Tristan Thompson — who is known in the tabloids for sharing two children with Khloé Kardashian — will produce “Satoshi” alongside Enderby Entertainment principals Rick Dugdale and Dan Petrie Jr.

“Satoshi” is among the first projects under a multi-picture deal between Enderby Entertainment and Saudi Arabia’s Yellow Camel Studios production company. The plan is to shoot the film at JAX Film Studios, a state-of-the-art production complex in the Saudi capital city of Riyadh.

The creator of Bitcoin, whose identity and invention remain secret, is also the subject of the Doug Liman-directed film “Bitcoin” (aka “Killing Satoshi”) which has a cast including Casey Affleck, Pete Davidson, Gal Gadot and Isla Fisher. “Bitcoin,” which is currently in post, has sparked controversy for using AI to create the movie’s sets and lighting, having been reportedly filmed in just 20 days inside a “gray box” studio in London.

Also on board “Satoshi” as producers are BDE Ventures founder and Bitcoin and cryptocurrencies pioneer Brian D. Evans, as well as actors Aaron Arnold (“Splitting Image”) and Austin Arnold (“Splitting Image,” “Altcoin Daily”), according to a statement from Enderby Entertainment.

articles.title: Josh O’Connor Describes Bond Rumors as ‘Incredibly Bizarre Pinch Me Moment’: ‘To Be Considered Is Extraordinary’
articles.summary: Josh O’Connor is the latest James Bond contender to address speculation surrounding the coveted role, calling the prospect of succeeding Daniel Craig an “incredibly bizarre pinch me moment.” The “Challengers” and “The Crown” actor, who is rumored to be one of the finalists in the search for the…
body: “It’s an incredibly bizarre pinch me moment…even being uttered in that same sentence and being considered for something like that,” O’Connor said while attending the opening of the Everyman Theatre’s new education and community center in his hometown of Cheltenham, England.
“To be considered in that same sort of bracket is extraordinary,” he added, before declining to elaborate on his potential involvement. “But I am afraid, there is nothing to say beyond that.”
O’Connor is reportedly among a handful of actors undergoing final screen tests for the role, alongside “Slow Horses” actor Jack Lowden and “Masters of the Air” actor Callum Turner.
Lowden also recently addressed the speculation, telling British GQ that the attention was “all very flattering” but that he wasn’t “going to add to the noise.”

articles.title: Creators Pounce on Midterm Elections, Hoping to Win New Viewers and More Dollars
articles.summary: Scott MacFarlane has traded in the desk once sat behind at CBS News on Election Night for something more direct — livestreamed midterms coverage for the progressive outlet MeidasTouch. He won’t have someone manipulating a Magic Wall or Big Board. He won’t be introduced by swelling orchestral music.
body: At a traditional TV outlet, says MacFarlane, his contribution would have been curated by producers. This year, he says, “the voice we get to use is my voice. I am going unscripted, without a teleprompter, just telling people point blank what’s happening.”

Coverage of returns on Election Night has long been dominated by the nation’s big TV-news outlets. This year, however, so-called “ creators ” — indie journalists and non-traditional experts — want their own piece of the audience.
Despite some of the hosts’ mainstream roots, many of them think they can bring viewers something the legacy outlets cannot.

“This will be Murdoch-Ellison-free coverage,” says Acosta of the show he and Couric plan to put on, making a direct nod to the ownership of Fox News by the Murdoch family and the control over CBS News and CNN now enjoyed by the Ellison family, which controls the newly formed Skydance. “Katie and I are free to let it rip.”

articles.title: Olga Kurylenko and Alex Pettyfer to Star in Crime Thriller ‘Breakwater,’ WestEnd Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Olga Kurylenko (“Quantum of Solace,” “Oblivion,” “Black Widow”) and Alex Pettyfer (“Magic Mike,” “The Butler,” “The Ministry of Ungentlemanly Warfare”) are set to star in crime thriller “Breakwater,” which has been boarded for world sales by WestEnd Films.
body: Set in a sun-soaked coastal paradise, “Breakwater” follows two women desperate for a way out. Iris (Kurylenko) is trapped in a toxic marriage, while Daya is a bartender desperate to escape her dead-end hometown.

A chance encounter brings them together, and they hatch a plan to blackmail Iris’ sadistic husband Avery (Pettyfer) aboard his luxury yacht. But what seems like the perfect escape quickly spirals out of control. Stranded on the high seas, with nowhere to run and no one to trust, Iris and Daya find their carefully laid plan turning into a fight for survival.

The film is produced by Kurt Wimmer (“The Beekeeper 1 & 2,” “Law Abiding Citizen,” “Point Break”), Jib Polhemus (“The Mechanic,” “Lara Croft: Tomb Raider,” “The Expendables 2”), Hannah Leader (“Mary,” “Freud’s Last Session,” “A Visit to Grandpa’s”) and Tad Daggerhart (“Black Lotus,” “Coyotes”), who also penned the script (“Expend4bles,” “Black Lotus”). James Ireland (“Echo Boomers”) executive produces for Dark Dreams Entertainment.

articles.title: Jury in Russell Brand rape trial begins considering verdicts
articles.summary: The media personality has been on trial for three weeks, after pleading not guilty to all charges.
body: The jury has begun considering the verdicts in Russell Brand's rape and sexual assault trial.
The media personality, 51, has been on trial at Southwark Crown Court in London for three weeks, facing three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault.
He has pleaded not guilty to all the charges. Giving evidence, he told the court he had been "obsessed" with sex in the past, but insisted it was always consensual.

The charges relate to allegations from six women spanning a decade between 1999 and 2009. Prosecutors said the complainants described him as someone who "didn't listen" when they said no, and "didn't care".

articles.title: Celebrity loses injunction bid but will stay anonymous pending appeal
articles.summary: The unnamed man asked for an injunction to stop his identity being reported in connection with allegations against him.
body: A celebrity who asked the High Court to permanently prevent two news organisations from publishing his identity and allegations of sexual misconduct has lost his case, with the court saying the man's claim for an injunction was denied.

But the judge Mr Justice Nicklin said a temporary injunction preventing the man from being named and the allegations published should remain in place, in order to allow the celebrity to appeal against the judgment, with anonymity and reporting restrictions remaining in force during the period allowed for any appeal.

ITN and the Guardian have said they believe it is in the public interest to publish allegations that the man abused his status to attempt or attempt to engage in "inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women".
The man, who denies the allegations, said any publication would be "highly likely" to lead him to kill himself, and that the court should prevent any publication or broadcast.

articles.title: Should California Subsidize Noah Wyle’s ‘The Pitt’ Pay?
articles.summary: Gov. Gavin Newsom’s $1 billion proposal to save Hollywood includes so-called "above-the-line” costs (a.k.a. big salaries) as qualified expenditures for a tax credit. That’s been a controversial idea in the state for a long time.
body: For nearly 20 years, California has drawn a line between subsidizing pay for people in front of the camera and the workforce behind it.

When the state started writing checks to Hollywood in 2009, the thinking was that the purpose of tax credits for films and TV shows would be to create jobs and juice the overall economy. That hasn’t changed through four iterations of the program across three governors. Its refusal to offset a production’s salary for, say, Tom Cruise, has made it an outlier among the 39 states that offer production incentives and is probably the biggest reason why it’s losing its grip as the filming capital of the world.

Now — in a major pivot from its historic position that allowing productions to count so-called “above-the-line” spending toward expenditures for filming subsidies would be irresponsible — California is doing the math. Select lawmakers have come to a not-so-surprising conclusion among industry insiders: the state can no longer afford not to.
“We’re still not competitive,” says Assemblymember Rick Chavez Zbur, a key legislator who has been working with Hollywood proponents to fine-tune the state’s incentive program.
